preconditions: The access requirements question is visible and No is selected.

assistiveTechnologyTests.procedure: Complete the journey and listen for the announcement or information under test.

title: Conditional question appears without an announcement
description: Selecting Yes to the access-requirements question reveals a follow-up field. The alpha path inserts it silently and leaves focus on the radio; nothing tells assistive-technology users that the page changed.

relatedElements.note: The beta path adds a role=status message and moves focus to the new field.

expectedBehaviour: New content that appears in response to input is announced, and focus does not leave the user without a cue that something changed.
actualBehaviour: The field appears with no live region, status message or focus change.
userImpact: Screen-reader users may answer No and continue without realising that an extra question appeared.

wcag.note: A change resulting from user input is not announced.

detection.note: Requires an interaction; the default page is identical in both paths.

observed.note: Page-level axe run with tags wcag2a, wcag2aa, wcag21a, wcag21aa and best-practice. No violation was reported in the default state; the control on the same page or path also passes.

manualTests: With a screen reader running, select Yes and listen for the new question.

assertions: No status region exists on the alpha path after the field is revealed.
tests: tests/journey-defects.spec.js: reveals the conditional question silently on the alpha path

reviewStatus.note: A Playwright regression test preserves the defective journey or widget behaviour and its control. That is automated reproduction, not a manual or assistive-technology observation.
